purpose: Valuation method reference for research roles. Use research data for current parameters and tool schemas for execution and report submission.
selectionBasis: Project guidance synthesized from the listed literature. Methods can be combined; business-type and lifecycle labels can overlap.

conventions.timing: Provide forecastStartDate and each period's endDate. Flows are full-period totals, assumed uniform within each period. Code removes elapsed portions and discounts at period-end; Gordon terminal value annualizes the final period's flow.
conventions.rates: Use decimals for rates and probabilities. Match cash-flow currency and nominal or real basis to the discount rate.
conventions.discounting: Execution uses ACT/365F: t=actual days from value date to cash-flow period-end/365; DF_t(r)=(1+r)^t. Supply a justified discount rate or CAPM/WACC components for code to combine.
conventions.commonEquityBridge: E_common=V_op+separately stated excess cash+other nonoperating assets-financing debt-preferred equity-applicable minority interests-other claims. Exclude excess cash from other assets; equity multiples require no further bridge.
conventions.perShare: P_common=E_common/N_common. Keep share count, share classes, employee options and financing treatment consistent; accounting diluted weighted-average shares may require adjustment.
conventions.missingInputs: Missing values are not zero. Record each assumption's basis and effect. Stop numerical valuation when essential inputs lack supportable assumptions.
conventions.terminalConstraint: Use perpetual terminal value only for a stable business with discount rate above growth. Code derives reinvestment, payout and residual income from growth and capital returns. For finite recovery, supply actual net recovery at the final date; RI subtracts ending book equity.
conventions.negativeEquity: Negative equity residuals are saved with diagnostics, without flooring at zero. Use them for solvency analysis, not target share prices; retain economically justified assumptions.
conventions.financialMetrics: financial.metrics precomputes TTM, quarterly, year-over-year, margin, cash-flow and equity comparisons. Read column definitions and periods; record forecasts separately from observations.

methods.name: Discounted free cash flow to the firm
requiredInputs: Forecast start and period-end dates, revenue, operating margin and realizable operating tax rate
Depreciation and amortization
Operating capital expenditure
Opening and period-end noncash operating working capital balances
WACC or its components
Stable return on capital and growth, or actual finite-horizon net recovery
Common-equity bridge and share count
useWhen: Nonfinancial operating cash flows and reinvestment can be modeled
Growth businesses can use multistage forecasts with negative early FCFF
invalidWhen: Operating liabilities and financing debt are undifferentiated, or cash-flow definitions are unresolved
Perpetual terminal value lacks a stable state or WACC_stable<=g
Essential capital expenditure is missing and EBITDA substitutes for FCFF
notes: Recognize tax benefits from losses only when realizable
Increases in NWC and Capex are cash outflows
Terminal value excludes the already modeled year-n cash flow
Bridge the result to common-equity value

methods.name: Discounted free cash flow to common equity
requiredInputs: Common net income after preferred-share claims
Depreciation, amortization and reinvestment
New borrowing and principal repayment schedule
Cost of equity
Stable growth and ROE, or finite-horizon net recovery; code derives retention
Share count consistent with contributions and share-class treatment
useWhen: Debt policy and shareholder capital requirements can be forecast explicitly
invalidWhen: Borrowing and repayment cannot be modeled
Equity cash flows are discounted at WACC
Perpetual terminal value has ke_stable<=g
notes: Borrowing is positive and repayment negative; net income already deducts interest
The result is equity value; do not subtract net debt again
Avoid double counting shareholder contributions funding negative FCFE and dilution from the same financing

methods.name: Common dividend discount model
requiredInputs: Common dividend or dividend-per-share schedule
Capital retention and distribution policy
Cost of equity
Stable growth
Share-count schedule for a per-share model
useWhen: Dividend forecasts match future payment capacity and capital needs
Mature distributing businesses or capital-constrained financial intermediaries
invalidWhen: Current zero dividends alone are used to infer permanent worthlessness
Stable model has ke<=g
Buybacks, issuance and share counts are duplicated or inconsistent
notes: Keep total common dividends and dividends per share distinct
The explicit forecast may include immature periods; stability is required for the terminal stage

methods.name: Regulatory-capital-constrained equity cash flow
requiredInputs: Common net income
Period-by-period business scale and risk-weighted assets or corresponding capital needs
Applicable capital constraints and management capital targets
Opening and period-end required common capital balances; code computes changes
Cost of equity
Terminal value consistent with capital needs and growth
useWhen: Financial intermediaries such as banks and insurers where operating liabilities are hard to separate from financing and equity retention can be forecast
invalidWhen: Applicable capital requirements and business forecasts are unavailable
Reported equity growth is treated directly as required capital growth
Operating inputs such as deposits are deducted as nonfinancial financing debt
notes: Capital releases must satisfy actual distribution constraints
Select by business economics and capital requirements, not a financial-sector label alone

methods.name: Common-equity residual income
formulas: CV_RI_n=RI_(n+1)/(ke_stable-g_RI) when residual income has stable perpetual growth
requiredInputs: Common book equity at forecast start and each period-end date
Period-by-period common earnings
Payout ratios, net issuance and book-equity reconciliation; code rolls equity to the value date
Other comprehensive income and accounting adjustments
Cost of equity
Terminal ROE and growth, or actual recovery; code derives residual income
useWhen: Book equity and earnings can be reconciled through clean surplus
Financial intermediaries or businesses where accounting capital supports earnings forecasts
invalidWhen: Book equity cannot be reconciled with earnings and shareholder transactions
Full terminal equity value is used as residual-income continuation value
Stable ROE/PB is applied to loss-making or intangible-intensive businesses without justification
notes: The book-capital charge uses opening equity
Perpetual residual-income growth need not equal revenue growth
Reconcile with DDM under consistent assumptions; this is not independent price evidence
Explicit-period dividends equal net income times payout ratio. Loss periods can have zero payout; a ratio cannot represent positive dividends during a loss. Explain funding for payout above 100%.

methods.name: Adjusted present value
requiredInputs: Unlevered operating cash flows and cost of capital
Debt, interest and principal repayment schedules
Realizable tax shields
Risk and discount assumptions for financing effects
Financing fees and distress losses excluded from operating forecasts
Common-equity bridge
useWhen: Financing structure changes materially and the debt schedule is explicit
Financing effects must be separated in leveraged transactions or restructuring
invalidWhen: Tax shields already priced in WACC are added again
Full tax deductions are assumed for unrealizable tax shields
Distress losses are deducted again after inclusion in operating forecasts
notes: Discount unlevered operations at the unlevered cost of capital
Tax rate times debt applies only under specific perpetuity assumptions
The tax-shield discount rate depends on debt policy and risk

methods.name: Comparable multiples
requiredInputs: Comparable companies and prices available at the valuation date
Positive, meaningful denominators covering the same forecast period
Growth, capital returns, risk, margins and accounting basis
Rationale for selected multiples and excluded peers
Common-equity bridge for EV-based models
useWhen: Companies have comparable operating and risk characteristics
As a primary model or independent market-pricing check, explicitly identified as relative valuation
invalidWhen: PE uses negative earnings or PB uses economically meaningless book equity
EV and share-price/market-cap numerators are mixed, or P/CF substitutes for EV/Revenue or EV/EBITDA
Key bases differ: historical versus forward, consolidated versus attributable, or gross versus net revenue
notes: Support multiples with company and peer economics rather than sector labels alone
Empirical fit to share prices does not validate intrinsic value
Explain margins, risk and reinvestment when using revenue multiples
Exit-multiple terminal values embed relative-pricing assumptions

methods.name: Adjusted net assets and liquidation value
requiredInputs: Asset inventory, fair values and ownership
Relevant liabilities, guarantees and other claims
Disposal conditions and recovery timing
Disposal taxes and costs
Valuation date and share count
useWhen: Real estate or investment holdings with separable assets
invalidWhen: Accounting net assets are treated directly as fair net assets
Orderly-disposal and forced-sale assumptions are mixed
Time value is omitted for distant disposals
Growth or brand value already priced in asset cash flows is added again
notes: May omit future investment opportunities
Allocate liquidation proceeds to common equity by claim priority

methods.name: Probability-weighted scenarios and R&D risk-adjusted NPV
formulas: V0=sum(s, p_s*V_s0) for mutually exclusive exhaustive scenarios on the same value and date basis
rNPV=sum(t, sum(s, P(state_s_at_t)*CF_s_t)/DF_t(r)) for an expected-cash-flow model
requiredInputs: Mutually exclusive, exhaustive scenarios or stage states and cash flows
Conditional and unconditional probabilities with supporting basis
Timing of revenue, costs and recovery
Remaining risk and discount rate
Claim allocation under financing and distress
Head-office costs and equity bridge when aggregating projects
useWhen: Early-stage businesses, R&D projects, transitions or distress have distinct outcome paths
Success probabilities, stage costs and commercial value can be justified
invalidWhen: Overlapping scenarios are added directly or probabilities are incomplete
All stage costs are multiplied by final success probability
Real-world probabilities use risk-free discounting without addressing remaining risk
The same technical failure loss is included in both probabilities and an extra discount-rate penalty
notes: Current committed expenditure has occurrence probability 1
Multiply path-conditional probabilities only when their definitions align
Model dependencies between correlated projects
Allocate common-equity proceeds within each scenario before taking expectations

methods.name: Real options
formulas: At each decision node compare continuation, investment, waiting and abandonment values, then value the chosen policy under consistent risk pricing.
requiredInputs: Executable decision rights and expiry dates
Stage investments and abandonment or recovery conditions
State variables, volatility and transition process
Future cash flows
Choice of real-world or risk-neutral measure and risk-pricing basis
useWhen: R&D, undeveloped resources or expansion allow decisions after new information arrives
Project states and actions can be modeled
invalidWhen: Uncertainty is high but no executable decision rights exist
Black–Scholes is applied mechanically to an untraded project
Option value is added after scenario valuation already includes optimal stopping
Real-world probabilities and risk-neutral discounting are mixed
notes: Use project-specific trees, lattices or simulation
The Schwartz source is the 2001 author manuscript; journal publication was in 2004

methods.name: Sum of the parts
requiredInputs: Segment financials and ownership
Applicable segment valuation methods and saved calculation IDs
Currency and a common valuation date
Segment and group debt allocation
Head-office expense forecasts, dates and discount rate, or explicit absence of such costs; intercompany transactions
Group common-equity claims and share count
useWhen: Group businesses differ materially in operations, risk and capital needs, with segment data available
invalidWhen: Segment operating values and equity values are added directly
Debt and head-office costs are deducted at both segment and group levels
Intercompany holdings or duplicated assets are not eliminated
A blanket conglomerate discount lacks justification
notes: This is an aggregation method; choose a base model for each segment
For segments valued from operations, complete one equity bridge at segment or group level

stageGuidance.focus: Milestones, stage investment, technical and commercial success probabilities, and financing.
Unit economics, customer acquisition and retention, and scaling conditions. Use multiples only with meaningful denominators and valid comparability.
Growth fade, margins, reinvestment, risk and financing paths.
Sustainable capital returns, reinvestment and distributions.
Finite life, contraction, asset disposal and closure costs. Justify any perpetual positive growth.

typeOverlays.constraint: Establish capital requirements and distributable earnings first. Use liability and debt definitions appropriate to financial intermediation.
Normalize margins and investment at current scale while retaining the near-term cycle path. Value finite reserves over their remaining life.
Treat intangible investment such as R&D consistently in earnings and capital; preserve investment when adding back expenses. Assess book-value comparability.
Distinguish inventory development, going-concern operations and asset disposal. Value assets and related liabilities within the same scope.
Weight costs and revenue by their own occurrence stages; count decision-right value once.
Model charges, maintenance investment, contract term and handover explicitly; supply applicable regulatory pricing rules for the project DCF.
Choose an applicable base model for each segment, align currency and claims, and allocate head-office items.
Distress can occur at any lifecycle stage. Model survival, restructuring or liquidation by scenario before allocating common-equity proceeds.
Estimate total value, then allocate under the specific contracts. The latest preferred-share price cannot price all common shares.
